channel.title: Sociology of Religion on Nikita Obraztsov
channel.description: Recent content in Sociology of Religion on Nikita Obraztsov

item.title: Stability, Silence, Community, and Psychotherapy: What Young People Are Looking for in Religion
item.description: English translation of a Forbes Young article by Elena Strelkova. On Gen Z religiosity in Russia and globally, featuring expert commentary.

item.title: What Does the Modern Person Believe? From Horoscopes to Neural Networks
item.description: Lecture transcript, Moscow, May 2026. On the contemporary religious situation, secularization theory, and the transformation of religion.

item.title: Parody Religions: From Discordia to the Flying Spaghetti Monster
item.description: Lecture transcript, Moscow, March 2026. On the sociology of parody religiosity — from Pastafarianism to Discordianism and the Church of the SubGenius.

item.title: The Concept of Belonging Without Believing in the Context of Orthodox Identity Formation in Russia
item.description: Conference paper presented at the VII All-Russian Sociological Congress, Moscow, November 2025. On the gap between declared Orthodox affiliation and actual religious practice in contemporary Russia.

item.title: Football as Quasi-Religion: A Scientific Analysis
item.description: Why Messi is called God, what football and religion have in common, and whether football is actually a religion. An analysis from the perspective of religious studies.

item.title: The Religiosity of Young People Today: Data and Interpretations
item.description: A paper presented at the XXX International Educational Readings. What sociological data tell us about the religiosity of young people in Russia and the United States — and how it differs from older generations.
